DVC management took longer  than expected. The delay in making the application for review is claimed to be bona fide, unintentional, and not  due to negligence on its part. Undoubtedly, the Commission under Regulation 69 of the <mark>2023 Conduct of Business Regulations</mark> is authorised to condone the delay in appropriate cases, on the Review Petitioner showing “sufficient reason”. We are also aware that a liberal approach needs to be adopted while considering such applications, to advance the cause of justice. We have considered the submissions of the Review Petitioner. We note that <mark>due to the technicalities of this case and the delay caused by the communication and exchange of necessary documents between the Review Petitioner’s counsel and the Review Petitioner, the Review Petition could not be filed within the specified time. Accordingly, we condone the  89-day delay in filing this Review Petition under Regulation 69 of the 2023 Conduct of Business Regulations.</mark>

- _(1) The Commission shall exercise jurisdiction to review its own orders, decisions, and directions in accordance with Clause (f) of sub-section (1) of Section 94 of the Act read with Section 114 and Order 47 of the Civil Procedure Code._

- _(2) Any person aggrieved by a direction, decision, or order of the Commission, from which no appeal has been preferred, may file a review petition on the following grounds within forty days of the making of such decision, direction, or order:_

_(a) by a decree or order from which an appeal is allowed, but from which no appeal has been preferred,_

_and who, from the discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence was not within his knowledge or could not be produced by him at the time when the decree was passed or order made, or on account of some mistake or error apparent on the face of the record or for any other sufficient reason, desires to obtain a review of the decree passed or order made against him, may apply for a review of judgment to the Court which passed the decree or made the order.”_

the Commission has the power to review its own orders, and this power is akin to Order 47 Rule 1 of the CPC.

Regarding the Review Petitioner's plea for clarification that the CEA Manual mandates approval only for additions to the Intra-STS at voltage levels of 66 kV and above, which have regional significance, we are of the view that this plea is outside the ambit of the review jurisdiction under Regulation 52 of the 2023 Conduct of Business Regulations and Order 47 Rule 1 of the CPC. Neither Regulation 52 of the 2023 Conduct of Business Regulations,  nor Order 47 Rule 1 of the CPC provides a mechanism for a mere "clarification" of an impugned order if it seeks to reargue the merits, alter the substantive findings, or supply a missing adjudication that does not stem from an accidental slip or clerical error.
